name: Shree Refrigerations Ltd
tagline: SME-listed defense/marine HVAC play riding shipbuilding and data-center-cooling tailwinds, but the technical/R&D story looks thin for the growth being guided
business_overview: Shree Refrigerations designs and manufactures chillers, refrigeration and HVAC systems for marine/naval (warship AC and refrigeration panels) and industrial applications, recently entering data-center cooling via a tie-up with Smardt. SME-board listed (IPO Aug 2025).
fundamentals_table: ~14.4% (one source cites 78% — likely a different base/period)
fundamentals_narrative: Genuinely strong revenue growth off a small base (FY25 revenue Rs 98.7 Cr, PAT Rs 13.5 Cr) with real order-book tailwinds (defense/shipbuilding capex, new data-center cooling vertical), but management guidance of 40-50% CAGR over 4-5 years is aggressive relative to the company's demonstrated engineering depth.
technical_read: Not independently pulled this pass — stock has been rallying on order-flow sentiment even without confirmed new order inflow as of the most recent post (2026-08-26).
sentiment_summary: Read the full thread (23 of 26 posts fetched, 2025-09 to 2026-08, single batch). Sentiment starts skeptical — multiple posters (Naresh, thevalueinvestor) flagged pre-IPO DRHP compliance issues (delayed GST/IT/PF filings) and questioned the 'technologically advanced' positioning given no visible engineering talent on LinkedIn and near-zero R&D spend (117 employees, no dedicated R&D line in the annual report). Sentiment turned more constructive from Mar 2026 as defense-sector order-book tailwinds (Mazagon Dock/Garden Reach corvette and submarine programs) and the Smardt data-center partnership gained traction, with management guiding 40-50% CAGR.
community_signal: Trusted user vivek_lakhani cautioned that for sub-Rs 2,000 Cr SME names with limited data history, conventional metrics and technicals are close to unusable — 'you just need to take leap of faith, believing in business & management' over a 3-5 year horizon. Trusted user Shail1234 engaged constructively on a related supplier (CFF Fluid Control) but flagged that management visibility (interviews, concalls, media presence) is thin across the SME defense-supplier space generally.

trusted_signals.note: Shared a pre-listing promoter interview without an explicit conviction call.

Cautioned that for a micro-cap SME (~684 Cr mcap, ~3,381 shareholders) with limited operating history, conventional fundamental/technical analysis is largely futile and investors need a multi-year 'leap of faith' on business and management quality instead.

bse_notes: DRHP risk-factor disclosures (pre-IPO) flagged delayed GST/Income Tax/PF filings as compliance weaknesses — not an active regulatory action, but a data point on internal-controls maturity for a company this age.
bull_case: Real, large addressable order-book tailwind: management cites >Rs 1 lakh Cr of upcoming corvette/submarine orders from Mazagon Dock and Garden Reach over the next few quarters
New data-center cooling vertical (Smardt tie-up) targets a fast-growing, capital-light adjacent market with an explicit ambition to be a top-3 India player
Genuine ~30% 3yr revenue CAGR and reasonable leverage (D/E ~0.36) even before the newer growth vectors ramp
bear_case: No visible engineering/R&D bench for a company positioning itself as 'technologically advanced' — multiple posters found no credentialed engineers on the team's LinkedIn profiles and no R&D spend line in the FY24 annual report
Pre-IPO compliance history (delayed GST/IT/PF filings) suggests immature internal controls for a company that has existed since 1990
Working capital is stretched (long cash-conversion cycle, low CFO/EBITDA per a SOIC-sourced summary) even as the stock re-rates on order-flow sentiment ahead of confirmed order inflow
Promoters draw ~Rs 2 Cr in combined salary/rent to family members, roughly 2% of revenue — a related-party-heavy compensation structure for this size of company
verdict_headline: Real defense/data-center order-book tailwinds, but the engineering depth and internal-controls maturity behind the growth guidance are both thin and largely unverified
verdict_reasoning: The sector tailwind (naval/shipbuilding capex, data-center cooling) and 30% trailing CAGR are specific and real enough to warrant a 10x-in-2-3-years tag, consistent with the project's inflection rule for small-caps with credible catalysts

But conviction should stay Low given the R&D/engineering-depth gap flagged directly by community due diligence, pre-IPO compliance weaknesses, and a trusted user's own caution that conventional analysis barely applies at this size and history
Worth revisiting once FY26/27 results test whether the 40-50% guided CAGR is achievable without the technical bench multiple posters could not verify

four_box.note: Naval/shipbuilding capex + new data-center cooling vertical (Smardt tie-up) is a real dual tailwind; management's 40-50% CAGR guide is aggressive relative to demonstrated depth — tam weak; multiple posters found no credentialed engineers/R&D spend for a company positioning as 'technologically advanced' — moat no; no valuation data recorded. Pre-IPO compliance history + related-party promoter compensation are separate governance flags.

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: ~68x trailing earnings prices management's 40-50% revenue CAGR guide (4-5 years) as delivered plus margin expansion; needs ~40%+ EPS CAGR held for years against a ~25-30x exit -- a demanding bar for a working-capital-heavy SME with a thin engineering bench
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: revenue +35-50% possible on naval/shipbuilding order flow and the Smardt data-center-cooling vertical if orders convert; PAT growth constrained by the ~377-day working-capital cycle and interest
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: highly contingent on the >Rs 1 lakh Cr corvette/submarine order pipeline actually converting to Shree orders and on building genuine engineering depth
market_expectation.gap_basis: the dual defence + data-center tailwind is real, but ~68x P/E prices flawless multi-year execution while ROCE has fallen to 13%, debtor days are ~251, FCF is negative, pre-IPO compliance was weak, and community due-diligence could not verify an R&D/engineering bench for the 'technologically advanced' positioning
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

track_record.note: Per screener.in (FY21-FY26): only FY23 (+13% revenue / ROCE 25%) and FY24 (+57% / ROCE 18%) cleared both bars; FY22 and FY25-FY26 had ROCE 13-14% despite strong revenue growth (working-capital-heavy, ~251 debtor days, ~377-day cycle). Listed only Aug 2025, so pre-IPO figures are DRHP-sourced.
